the 10-year cumulative incidence of HBC was 1.70% in Korean patients with chronic hepatitis B who were in the immune tolerant or early immune active phase and had no or minimal liver fibrosis.

(1) a high serum HBV DNA gradient (defined as the difference between serum HBV DNA levels measured in the same patient at two timepoints, divided by the average of these levels, and multiplied by 100) was associated with the risk of remaining in the immune tolerant state of chronic hepatitis B; (2) the 10-year cumulative incidence of hepatoma in patients with immune-tolerant chronic hepatitis B without significant liver fibrosis was low;

the cumulative incidence of HBC at 10 years was low in young patients with IT phase CHB, but was significantly associated with a high serum viral load and a low serum ALT level, and the risk of HBC was higher in those who remained in the IT phase for 5 years than in those who changed to HBeAg-negative CHB.

the IT phase of CHB is not a static phase, and that it can be predicted with a high degree of certainty whether or not a patient will leave the phase within a certain period of time.
